registered_before: any with/without-rules number on pulse-peer-discount-confirm (no Falco, tripwire or triage number of that run has been computed)
why: ML is complete (Pulse 5.27): the stable ML is policy-k2of2-a5-peer30, confirmed live on pulse-peer-discount-confirm. Amendment 1 named 'the confirmation live run' as primary data; this fixes which one and the details amendment 1 left open.

data.primary: pulse-peer-discount-confirm (the live run of the final stable ML; campaign blind for every arm)
data.secondary: pulse-stable-confirm with arm A = the stable rule recomputed on its window table (blind test of 5.22); reported, not used for any conclusion
data.development: pulse-stable-candidate / pulse-stable-refreshed as in amendment 1 (aggregates only)

arm_A: the live previews of policy-k2of2-a5-peer30 (window table column 'preview'; agreement with the offline rule 99.9999 %, Pulse 5.27)
normal_span: the same for every arm: from the end of the run's selection span (the tripwire reference) to the end of the capture, campaign span excluded (burden_levers.campaign_span); replica-hours from the ML window table on that span
tripwire_B2: rule of R3 (tripwire-a1-blind-v1): a window has an alert when it carries a syscall ID absent from its workload's reference and outside the frozen exec set E (validation-evidence/results-20261021/pulse-stable-candidate/final/exec-set-E.json, sha256 a3266613...); reference = the union of IDs per workload over the run's selection span; trial detected when a window inside [start, start + 15 s] has an alert
falco_B1: falco_baseline.py definitions unchanged (event of the trial container inside [start, start + 15 s]; normal events of production containers)
triage_B3: rule_tier.py definitions unchanged (episode held back when every RCA case of its container with trigger window_end within 5 s is probe-only; trial held back when all cases within [start, start + 20 s] are probe-only; fail-open); declared probes: validation-evidence/results-20261021/exec-probe-spec.json
container_key: (pod_uid, container_name); Falco's pod name is mapped to pod_uid with the run's resolver metadata (worker issues.jsonl); Falco events of unmapped containers count under (pod name, container name)
latency: first alert of the arm - kernel_event_at, attacks only; for B3 the alert time of a paged trial is the creation time of its RCA case (the triage decision) when it has one, else the preview time (fail-open), and the number of fail-open trials is reported
comparison: unchanged from amendment 1: every B arm against A on the same trials and normal span; paired per-trial differences with a workload-clustered bootstrap 95 % CI (10,000 draws); burden difference with the same bootstrap; p95 difference with a bootstrap over attack trials
code: scripts/analysis/rule_comparison.py (new), novel_syscalls.py --normal-span and per-trial output, falco_baseline.py container names on normal events
